data.narrative: Module 2 (Reading Logs) - the student read live request/response log pairs, verified UTC timestamp normalization across app and DB, then discovered a forged admin-login log line embedded inside a user-controlled URL field. They recognized it as log injection, hardened the logging boundary with control-character sanitization, and locked the fix with a regression test.

dimension_scores.observation: Hypothesized the forged line was log injection (user-controlled newline + crafted JSON) from log structure alone before touching code.
dimension_scores.evidence: Correctly inferred the r-102 admin login had no matching request-received event and sat inside r-101's url value.

dimension_scores.observation: Reconstructed the full request timeline from live logs - login (200, 235.6ms), link create (201, 41.9ms), missing link (404, 16.5ms) - and spotted the temporal anomaly of the embedded forged entry.
dimension_scores.evidence: Observed log timeline: request received -> response sent pairs with duration_ms for every request; identified the orphan r-102 event.

dimension_scores.observation: Built a deterministic regression test feeding the exact incident payload into _log and asserting single-line JSON output.
dimension_scores.evidence: tests/test_log_injection.py replays the newline+admin-login URL and asserts url field has no \n/\r.

dimension_scores.observation: Explained the forged entry clearly: evidence in the log itself (no request-received for r-102), the trust-boundary consequence, and the required fix.
dimension_scores.evidence: Summary: the admin login is FORGED - embedded inside prior line's url field; logs are a trust boundary.

dimension_scores.observation: Root-caused to the boundary: user-controlled data interpolated into log output without escaping control characters - not a 'bad log line' but a vulnerability class.
dimension_scores.evidence: Fix at logging boundary (app/main.py _sanitize strips [\x00-\x1f\x7f]); identified that any external data crossing into logs must be sanitized like SQL.

dimension_scores.observation: Module exercises postmortem lightly; student connected the lesson to a reusable rule (ask if every new log line logs user data and is sanitized) but did not write a formal postmortem.
dimension_scores.evidence: REFLECT answers named risk (forged logs hide tracks) and mitigation (sanitize user data at the logging boundary).

strengths: Detected the forged admin-login line from log structure alone (no request-received for r-102, embedded in r-101's url field) - genuine log literacy.
Applied the fix at the logging boundary with control-character sanitization, not at a single call site - closes the whole class.
Locked the fix with a regression test replaying the exact incident payload.
growth_areas: Postmortem framing is thinner than the other dimensions - a one-paragraph blameless writeup (impact, root cause, remediation) would round out this module.
data.recommendation: For Module 3 (Reproduction), write a minimal repro script first and confirm it fails before changing any code - the deterministic-repro habit will pay off on the intermittent bugs.

public_evidence.artifact: Logging boundary hardening in app/main.py + regression test tests/test_log_injection.py
public_evidence.student_action: Fixed a log-injection vulnerability by sanitizing user-controlled fields before they reach the structured log stream, and verified the fix with a regression test.
public_evidence.technical_detail: app/main.py _log now passes every field through _sanitize() which strips control characters (newline, CR) from string values before json.dumps output; tests/test_log_injection.py replays the attacker URL.
public_evidence.proof: pytest tests/test_log_injection.py -> pass; captured log line renders the whole malicious URL as a single value: 'https://normal-url.com {"ts"..."admin login successful"...}' with no newlines.
public_evidence.ability: Finds and closes security vulnerabilities at the right layer
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows a security vulnerability was found (log forging via newline injection), root-caused to unsanitized user data crossing a trust boundary, and fixed with a regression guard - not a symptom patch.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Detected the forged admin login embedded in a URL value and fixed the boundary sanitization.
Verified DB timezone UTC, timestamptz columns, and matching aware UTC values for now() and created_at.
Rebuilt login/create/404 timelines from request-received/response-sent pairs with duration_ms.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used the incident log excerpt itself as evidence (orphan req_id, embedded JSON) before any code
